assessment_summary: In step 0062, the author deduces that the condition $f \le 4$ 'leaves only the case $p=5$'. However, $f$ was defined in step 0052 as $(p-1)/2$ for a prime $p > 3$. The inequality $f \le 4$ means $(p-1)/2 \le 4$, which implies $p \le 9$. The primes greater than 3 satisfying this are $p=5$ (where $f=2$) and $p=7$ (where $f=3$). Because $p=7$ is also a valid case that satisfies $f \le 4$, the claim that it leaves ONLY $p=5$ is mathematically incorrect, making this step flawed.
